assays.assay_description: Mice traversed an enclosed glass-plate runway in a darkened environment; 5-min recording session starting 5 min after i.p. DOM injection. Multiple gait parameters extracted: speed, cadence, stride length, stance/swing time, contact area, plantar pressure, support patterns, base of support, print positions, phase dispersions. Includes pharmacological pretreatment arms with MDL100907 (5-HT2A antagonist) and SB242084 (5-HT2C antagonist).

application_type.evidence: All drugs were administered intraperitoneally (i.p.) at a volume of 10 ml/kg body weight

setup_habituation.evidence: The mice were habituated to the experimental environment for 5-7 days. They were trained on the CatWalk system for at least 3 days before the experiment

setup_restrain.evidence: mice were placed on the runway for 5 min; CatWalk measures gait in a natural state

food_restriction.evidence: Food and water were available ad libitum (home cage); no food in CatWalk runway during the 5-min recording

water_restriction.evidence: Food and water were available ad libitum (home cage); no water in CatWalk runway during the 5-min recording

time_to_assay.evidence: mice were placed into the behavioral apparatus 5 min after an i. p. Injection of DOM

sample_size.evidence: (n = 12, mean ± SEM, one-way ANOVA compared with the saline group)

outcomes.summary: DOM (0.3-3 mg/kg) dose-dependently increased locomotor velocity by shortening step cycle (mainly reduced stance) and increasing stride length and swing speed (~47% increase in average speed at 1 mg/kg). DOM also decreased mean plantar pressure, reduced forepaw print areas, decreased base of support, and increased temporal regularity of paw placement. MDL100907 (0.1 mg/kg, 5-HT2A antagonist) normalized DOM-induced gait alterations, whereas SB242084 (1 mg/kg, 5-HT2C antagonist) did not. 10 mg/kg DOM suppressed voluntary locomotion, reversible by 5-HT2C antagonism.
outcomes.evidence: DOM treatment reduced duration (F(3,44)=8.401, P=0.0002) and elevated cadence and average speed... The average speed showed a 47 % increase compared with the saline control group.

assays.assay_description: Forced treadmill gait analysis (DigiGait system) at fixed 12 cm/s with no incline, used to assess whether 10 mg/kg DOM impaired motor capacity when voluntary CatWalk locomotion was suppressed.

application_type.evidence: All drugs were administered intraperitoneally (i.p.) at a volume of 10 ml/kg body weight

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice ran on treadmill at fixed velocity; no physical restraint described

food_restriction.evidence: Treadmill apparatus has no food access during the test

water_restriction.evidence: Treadmill apparatus has no water access during the test

time_to_assay.evidence: Same dosing window as CatWalk; mice tested shortly after 10 mg/kg DOM injection

sample_size.evidence: Details in Supplementary Table 1; n not specified in main text

outcomes.summary: At 10 mg/kg DOM, mice that could not voluntarily traverse the CatWalk runway still maintained the ability to run at a constant speed on the DigiGait treadmill, indicating preserved motor capacity and suggesting the locomotor suppression reflects reduced motivation rather than motor impairment.
outcomes.evidence: the mice maintained the ability to run at a constant speed on the treadmill in the passive gait (DigiGait) analysis system even at this dose (Supplementary Table 1)

B1_num_measures.evidence: Main text reports only ability to run at a constant speed

B4_ethological.evidence: Forced treadmill locomotion is not a species-typical ethological behaviour

D2_session_duration.evidence: Duration not specified; standard DigiGait runs are brief

judge_notes: Two assays retained: CatWalk voluntary gait analysis (main study, all doses + 5-HT2A/2C antagonist arms collapsed into one assay per rubric) and DigiGait forced treadmill (distinct apparatus and paradigm, used for 10 mg/kg DOM).

B3 scored 1 for CatWalk: phase dispersions and 6-pattern gait sequence distribution constitute analysis of sequential/transitional structure between paws within step cycles — overriding two candidates that scored 0.
B4 scored 0 for CatWalk: gait kinematics are motor parameters, not species-typical ethological acts (grooming, social investigation, USVs). Overrides gptoss which scored 1.
B7 scored 0: CatWalk XT and DigiGait are commercial pressure/position-tracking systems, not pose-estimation or supervised behaviour classifiers.
Housing enrichment scored not_reported (low confidence) — paper is silent; overrides gptoss which inferred 'no'.
Food/water_restriction = 'during' for both assays: paper states ad libitum food/water in home cage and apparatus clearly excludes food/water during the short test.
